description: Scientific and technical answer grounding and citation benchmark across 8 research intents.

queries.query: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation and how does it combine parametric and non-parametric memory?
expected_dimensions: parametric memory generator
non-parametric memory dense retriever
differentiable end-to-end training
marginalization over latent documents

queries.query: How does Dense Passage Retrieval index documents and score question-passage pairs using dual encoders?
expected_dimensions: dual-encoder architecture
dense representations
dot-product similarity
in-batch negative training

queries.query: What is the scaled dot-product attention formula in the Transformer architecture?
expected_dimensions: scaled dot-product attention formula
query, key, value projections
division by square root of key dimension
softmax normalization

queries.query: What is Sentence-BERT and how does it compute semantically meaningful sentence embeddings?
expected_dimensions: siamese network architecture
mean pooling over token embeddings
triplet loss objective
fast cosine similarity search

queries.query: What is Reciprocal Rank Fusion and what formula does it use to combine ranked lists?
expected_dimensions: rank reciprocal formula
smoothing parameter k (typically 60)
score calibration independence
combining multiple retrieval systems

queries.query: Explain how RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token models differ in their document marginalization mechanisms.
expected_dimensions: RAG-Sequence marginalizes over fixed document for entire sequence
RAG-Token allows different latent documents per generated token
beam search decoding variations
joint generation probability

queries.query: Explain why multi-head attention allows transformers to jointly attend to information at different representation subspaces.
expected_dimensions: linear projections to query, key, value dimensions
parallel attention heads
representation subspaces
concatenation and output projection

queries.query: Explain why cross-encoder rerankers achieve higher accuracy than dual-encoders but have higher computational latency.
expected_dimensions: full cross-attention between all query and document tokens
lack of precomputable index for cross-encoders
dual-encoder independent representation caching
two-stage retrieval architecture trade-off
queries.ground_truth_source: Karpukhin et al., 2020 & Reimers et al., 2019

queries.query: Compare BM25 lexical keyword retrieval versus Dense Passage Retrieval on vocabulary mismatch and exact keyword matching.
expected_dimensions: BM25 term frequency-inverse document frequency matching
BM25 sensitivity to vocabulary mismatch and synonymy
DPR semantic vector similarity in latent space
DPR weakness with rare entities and out-of-vocabulary acronyms
hybrid retrieval complementary strengths
queries.ground_truth_source: Karpukhin et al., 2020 & Cormack et al., 2009

queries.query: Compare bi-encoder architectures like Sentence-BERT with cross-encoder rerankers in terms of scoring latency and token interaction.
expected_dimensions: bi-encoder independent passage embedding offline indexing
cross-encoder joint query-passage input concatenation
O(1) vector index search vs O(N) forward-pass cross-encoder inference
token interaction depth across layers

queries.query: Compare Reciprocal Rank Fusion RRF against Relative Score Fusion RSF for hybrid retrieval candidate merging.
expected_dimensions: RRF rank-only position independence without score normalization
RSF min-max score normalization requirement
robustness to uncalibrated dense and BM25 score distributions
weighting parameter alpha impact

queries.query: Why does dense semantic retrieval fail when queries contain novel product codes or unseen medical entity identifiers?
expected_dimensions: out-of-vocabulary tokenization and subword fragmentation
unseen embedding cluster dispersion in latent space
lack of exact string matching guarantee in dense dot-products
mitigation via hybrid lexical search

queries.query: Why does the Transformer scale the dot products by 1/sqrt(d_k) before applying the softmax function?
expected_dimensions: dot products grow large in magnitude for large d_k
large values push the softmax function into regions of extremely small gradients
division by sqrt(d_k) counteracts variance scaling
prevents gradient vanishing during backpropagation

queries.query: How to implement a two-stage hybrid retrieval pipeline combining BM25, dense embeddings, and cross-encoder reranking?
expected_dimensions: stage 1 parallel BM25 and dense index querying
stage 1 candidate fusion via Reciprocal Rank Fusion
candidate deduplication and top-N extraction
stage 2 cross-encoder batch reranking
evidence packaging and MMR diversity selection
queries.ground_truth_source: Lewis et al., Karpukhin et al., Cormack et al.

queries.query: How does deterministic citation verification validate that LLM generated claims are grounded in evidence passages?
expected_dimensions: claim extraction and citation ID linking
passage token overlap and semantic similarity checks
support status classification (SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, UNSUPPORTED)
source URL and document ID metadata provenance verification
queries.ground_truth_source: Lewis et al., 2020 & AI Research Copilot Verification Engine

queries.query: How do attention mechanisms in Transformer sequence-to-sequence generators enable grounded synthesis over retrieved documents in RAG?
expected_dimensions: dense passage retrieval produces top candidate documents
cross-attention layers attend to concatenated input context and question
autoregressive decoding conditioned on non-parametric memory
marginalization over latent document distributions
queries.ground_truth_source: Lewis et al., 2020 & Vaswani et al., 2017

queries.query: How does combining Dense Passage Retrieval with BM25 using Reciprocal Rank Fusion improve retrieval over individual retrievers?
expected_dimensions: BM25 captures exact lexical keywords and terminology
DPR captures paraphrased semantic meaning
RRF integrates distinct rank distributions without score scale biases
higher recall@K and lower zero-hit rates across diverse query types
queries.ground_truth_source: Karpukhin et al., 2020 & Cormack et al., 2009

queries.query: How does fine-tuning Sentence-BERT embeddings with triplet loss improve dense candidate generation for cross-encoder rerankers?
expected_dimensions: triplet loss optimizes relative distance between anchor, positive, and negative
sentence embeddings cluster semantically in vector space
higher quality top-N candidate pool passed to downstream rerankers
cross-encoder acts on high-precision candidates to yield final rank ordering

queries.query: What are the primary dense retrieval architectures for open-domain question answering and knowledge retrieval?
expected_dimensions: dual-encoder models (DPR, SBERT)
late-interaction multi-vector models (ColBERT)
generative retrieval models
hybrid dense-lexical architectures
queries.ground_truth_source: Karpukhin et al., Reimers et al., Lewis et al.

queries.query: What are the standard reranking paradigms used in multi-stage information retrieval systems?
expected_dimensions: pointwise cross-encoders
pairwise ranking networks
listwise cross-encoders and neural rankers
LLM-based sliding window and prompting rerankers
queries.ground_truth_source: Medical Reranker Paper & Karpukhin et al.

queries.query: What is the taxonomy of retrieval-augmented generation architectures across naïve, advanced, and modular RAG?
expected_dimensions: naïve RAG retrieve-then-read approach
advanced RAG with query pre-retrieval routing and post-retrieval reranking
modular RAG with iterative routing and multi-hop decomposition
claim-level citation and verification mechanisms
queries.ground_truth_source: Lewis et al., 2020 & RAG Evolution Literature

queries.query: What are the recent trends in modular RAG architectures regarding multi-source query decomposition and verification?
expected_dimensions: query intelligence and intent-driven decomposition
parallel multi-source retrieval across academic, web, and code sources
evidence deduplication and maximal marginal relevance selection
hallucination mitigation via deterministic citation audits
queries.ground_truth_source: Lewis et al. & Modern RAG Architecture Survey

queries.query: What are the emerging trends in neural rerankers regarding latency optimization and quantization?
expected_dimensions: cross-encoder distillation into lightweight models (MiniLM)
INT8/FP16 quantization for CPU and edge inference
two-stage cascade reranking to reduce candidate pool size
token pruning and early exit strategies

queries.query: What are the key industry trends in hallucination reduction and citation grounding for scientific AI assistants?
expected_dimensions: claim-level attribution and structured JSON synthesis
post-generation deterministic citation verification
unsupported claim pruning and confidence scoring
interactive provenance tracking linking claims to source documents
queries.ground_truth_source: Lewis et al. & Grounded AI Literature

queries.query: How do parameter scaling laws and non-parametric retrieval corpus size affect factual accuracy in RAG systems?
expected_dimensions: scaling non-parametric corpus expands factual knowledge base without model retraining
parametric memory scaling improves reasoning and synthesis fluency
trade-off between corpus retrieval latency and generator size
knowledge update efficiency via index updates
queries.ground_truth_source: Lewis et al., 2020 & Scaling Laws Literature
